_doc: RATIFIED DIVERGENCES + JUDGMENT-CALL CORRECTIONS. Two lists. `divergences` = places where our corpus text DELIBERATELY differs from what the source page legibly prints, each ratified. `pending_review` = corrections made on Claude's own contextual judgment (with outside knowledge, as sanctioned) and awaiting Luneth's end-of-campaign sweep. WHY IT EXISTS: on 2026-08-02 a vision sweep re-flagged WAL-CLM-LETS-000349 (toxin/antitoxin) and WAL-CLM-IMMORT-000024 (1n/1nm) as defects. BOTH had already been ruled on and corrected in earlier sessions, and neither was written down -- so each was re-derived at the cost of a render, a 20x-40x read and an adversarial second read. Luneth: 'we already fixed this ... note it this time so this doesn't need to be re-derived.'
_the_rule: The page is EVIDENCE, not ground truth. Luneth 2026-08-02: 'the books are RIDDLED with errors ... we NEED outside information to correct it -- what we DON'T correct is true Wallach statements even if his statements disagree with outside norms, what we DO fix is when there's a clear typo or error.' So a genuine Wallach claim stands even against mainstream fact; a typesetter's or scanner's error gets fixed, using outside knowledge, and gets logged HERE for his review.
_internal_only: A verification-audit artifact. Read by tooling only. MUST NOT be surfaced to the user, rendered on any app surface, or folded into a derived artifact. Nothing under eden/tools/ is consumed by corpus_derive/build_embeds/build.mjs -- verified 2026-08-02 -- and that must stay true.
_standard: Each entry states what OUR text holds, what the PAGE prints, WHO decided, WHEN, and the EVIDENCE. An entry without a decider and a reason is not a ratified divergence -- it is an undisclosed change, which is the defect class this file prevents.

divergences.reason: A 1000x misprint carried identically by all four books. 400 mg of elemental silver daily causes argyria and silver toxicity; Youngevity's own colloidal-silver products deliver 13-40 MCG, corroborating mcg as intended. Corrected under the dose-misprint safety mandate: safety outranks byte-faithfulness for a dose a reader could act on. NEVER restore the printed 400 mg.
divergences.evidence: Recorded in memory dose-misprint-safety-mandate; all three ids re-measured 2026-08-02 and each still carries the corrected figure. WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000064 was in the same 2026-07-21 sweep but its verbatim no longer contains the figure, so nothing there can regress.
divergences.proven_useful: 2026-08-02: a vision agent hit IMMORT-000027, checked this list, and returned DOCTRINE_OK instead of proposing a restore to 400 mg.

divergences.reason: The treatment is tetanus ANTItoxin (the neutralising antiserum). The page's 'toxin' is a book misprint that, left standing in a protocol a reader could act on, describes administering the poison. Luneth: 'We already fixed this, ours is correct, it's antitoxin.' The earlier fix was never logged, which is why this file exists.
divergences.evidence: Page read 2026-08-02 at 14x-20x (lets-play-doctor PDF p157 = printed p145): no hyphens, no parentheses, no 'anti' prefix -- the line literally begins 'fixed toxin,'. The divergence is real and deliberate, not an OCR artifact on either side.
divergences.do_not_confuse: The same claim carried a genuine OCR defect, FIXED 2026-08-02 and not a divergence: 'rv q6 h' -> 'IV q6 h'.

divergences.ours: vitamin A at 25,000-300,000 IU per day as beta carotene
divergences.page_prints: vitamin C at 25,000-300,000 IU per day as beta carotene
divergences.reason: Beta carotene is the vitamin A precursor and 25,000-300,000 IU is an A dose, so 'vitamin C ... as beta carotene' is internally incoherent. The LEFT column of the same page prints 'vitamin A at 25,000-300,000 IU per day as beta carotene' with identical wording; the tonsillitis entry's 'C' is duplicated down from the preceding clause 'vitamin C to bowel tolerance'.
divergences.evidence: Page read 2026-08-02 at 16x (lets-play-doctor PDF p184 = printed p172): the glyph is an unambiguous C, matching the C in 'vitamin C to bowel tolerance' two words earlier.
divergences.do_not_confuse: The same claim carried a genuine OCR defect, FIXED 2026-08-02: 'Verataim viride' -> 'Veratrum viride'.

divergences.reason: The passage defines nanotechnology, where the unit is the nanometre. Luneth: 'we did the work before and nm is correct when talking about nanotechnology, clearly.' Another correction made in an earlier session and never logged -- re-derived from scratch on 2026-08-02, which is the cost this file removes.
divergences.evidence: Page read 2026-08-02 at 36-40x (immortality Screenshot (58), right half, printed p91): the page really does print the bare 'n', with a real 'm' one line above proving an 'm' would have been visible. Three sibling books print the bare 'n' too (rare-earths, hk, epigenetics) -- so the divergence is OURS and deliberate, applied to immortality only.
divergences.open_item: The other three books still carry the bare '1n to 100n'. Making them consistent is a judgment call not yet taken; flagged rather than silently swept.

divergences.ratified_by: Claude, under Luneth's explicit delegation 2026-08-02 ('use context to figure it out yourself whether gm or mg is correct')
divergences.reason: gm is correct and our text already holds it. Cartilage is a bulk supplement dosed in grams; 5 mg t.i.d. is a pharmacologically meaningless quantity. The SAME book prints 'cartilage at 5 gm t.i.d.' twice more -- WAL-CLM-LETS-000326 (joint pain, printed p139) and WAL-CLM-LETS-000435 (sprains, printed p169) -- and printed p139 also carries '5 gm flaxseed oil t.i.d.', so gm is this book's normal unit for bulk supplements. The carpal-tunnel entry's 'mg' is the book contradicting itself.
divergences.evidence: printed p139 read by eye 2026-08-02 (gm, confirmed); p169 corroborated by the PDF text layer agreeing with our gm; the p111 'mg' page-read twice at 22x by independent agents. NO SOURCE CHANGE WAS MADE -- our text was already correct.
divergences.why_it_nearly_went_wrong: A uniform 'fix all three occurrences of 5 gm' sweep would have rewritten two page-faithful values. The corroboration instrument distinguished them correctly: p111 disagreed between the two OCR passes, p151 and p181 agreed.

divergences.reason: The geneticist's name is Hamer. Luneth ruled that correcting this is in scope and that hesitating over it was pedantic: the books are riddled with errors of exactly this kind and outside information is required to fix them. What is NOT corrected is a true Wallach statement that disagrees with outside norms.
divergences.evidence: Page-read 2026-08-02; the page prints 'Harmer'. Kept as ours.

pending_review._doc: Corrections applied on Claude's contextual judgment, using outside knowledge as Luneth sanctioned on 2026-08-02, and awaiting his end-of-campaign review sweep: 'these fixes should be noted for my review when they occur so I can do a review sweep at the end just in case you over-reach on this.' Every one was also seen on the page; the judgment is in the INTERPRETATION, not in whether the glyphs were read.

batch_2026-08-02.basis: the printed list runs Vitamin A / 81 / B2 / B3 / B5 / B6 / B12 / C / D / [blank] / K -- the sequence itself fixes 81 as B1
same list; the only vitamin missing between D and K is E, dropped by OCR
subscript digit read as a comma; the book's own preceding line names niacin, and niacin is B3
subscript 50 read as letters; LD50 is the standard toxicology term
page-read at 22x: subscript 12 read as two commas AND the following comma read as 'i'

capital I read as lowercase l. DELIBERATELY SPARED: a sixth occurrence, 'the chemical symbol of Gl' for GLUCINUM (the old name for beryllium), whose symbol really was Gl -- a blanket Gl->GI would have corrupted a correct chemical symbol
the botanical name of green hellebore; page-read at 8x confirms Veratrum
page-read; ru read as m, rri read as m. Both were invisible to the corroboration pass because the second OCR shared the same error
tight justification; four spaces dropped by OCR. The letter-letter dropped-space class, previously recorded as unmeasured
page-read at 34x: the mark has a descender (comma), and a period on the same page renders as a compact dot. Ours silently promoted a mid-sentence clause into a new sentence
sentence-final period read as a comma
the page uses curly, and the adjacent 'isn’t' in the same sentence pair is already curly in our own text -- a local inconsistency, not a corpus-wide convention change
rr read as th; closing curly quote read as straight ASCII
d read as t
q read as g
c read as e
page-read at 20x: two strokes, not three
page-read at 16x; the second is a mid-sentence line break, so the capital was ours
two spaces dropped by OCR
page-read at 20x; the line above prints 'two million u IV q 6 h' in the same form

line-break hyphens rejoined only where the two halves concatenate into a real word; 1 kept its lexical hyphen. Scope held to front-facing verbatims -- the book carries 1650 such wraps overall and whole-book repair is out of mandate

batch_2026-08-02_nonword._doc: Wave 3, the non-word self-scan. 105 tokens page-read; 62 confirmed LEGITIMATE and left alone, 18 were OCR garbles in OUR text, 22 were typos the PAGE ITSELF carries. The BOOK_TYPO set below is the one needing Luneth's eye: the page is faithful and we corrected it anyway, under the standing uniform-correction ruling. Any of them can be reverted.

book_typos_corrected.flag: SEMANTIC — barytes is barium sulfate. Worth your eye; the correction is inferred from the substance, not just the spelling.
a split botanical name — the genus is Leonurus (motherwort)
SEMANTIC — the sweetener is aspartame; 'Aspartamine' is not a substance. Corrected from meaning, not spelling. Worth your eye.

judgment_calls.basis: The page really does print it RUN TOGETHER — unlike WAL-CLM-LETS-000510's occurrence 400 chars away, which has the space and was a genuine OCR drop. Tight justification squeezed this word space to nothing. Corrected as a typesetting artifact because 'typical ofdiarrhea' is not a word of Wallach's, but the page is faithful, so this is the most reversible entry in the batch.

A SECOND occurrence of the same r-read-as-i failure, on a different page from the one that was page-verified (WAL-CLM-LETS-000398). Fixed from context without its own page read — 'dietaiy' is not a word in any language and 'dietary fiber' is unambiguous. Re-reading a page to confirm that is the pedantry you flagged.

The page prints 'en-' / 'hanced' across a line break; our OCR dropped the HYPHEN as well, leaving a bare newline inside the word. That makes it invisible to the hyphen gate, which requires a hyphen to be present — a hyphen-LESS line-break split, a class with no detector yet.

_classes.note: The scanned glyph 'meg' is genuinely ambiguous between mg and mcg. Resolving it to mcg is reading the page, not departing from it; 126 such fixes are recorded in memory dose-misprint-safety-mandate. Listed so a future pass does not mistake the class for a divergence -- but the UNIT MUST STILL BE READ OFF THE RENDER per claim, never inferred from what a dose ought to be.
Digit 1 misread for lowercase L in 'betaine HCl'. Book-wide OCR artifact, corrected uniformly.

Under correct-everything-uniformly the books' own typos are corrected uniformly, INCLUDING inside the verbatim. Verified by eye on rare-earths printed p329, which really prints 'flourosis', 'flouride' x3, 'flouridation'. The class is large -- 278 hunks measured 2026-08-02 across the five unverified books -- and does not belong in a per-claim list.
